question.prompt: For any complex number \(w=a+bi,\) \(|w|\) is defined to be the real number \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2}.\) If \(w=\cos40^\circ+i\sin40^\circ,\) then \[ |w+2w^2+3w^3+\cdots+9w^9|^{-1} \] equals

solutions.explanation:
The angle \(40^\circ\) makes the powers repeat after nine factors. Indeed, the sine and cosine addition formulas show that multiplying \(\cos\alpha+i\sin\alpha\) by \(\cos\beta+i\sin\beta\) adds their angles. Therefore
\[
w^9=\cos360^\circ+i\sin360^\circ=1.
\]
Also \(|w|=1\), and \(w\ne1\) because \(\sin40^\circ>0\).

First let \(G=w+w^2+\cdots+w^9\). Subtracting its one-power shift gives
\[
(1-w)G=w-w^{10}=0,
\]
since \(w^{10}=w\). As \(1-w\ne0\), we have \(G=0\).

Now let \(S=w+2w^2+\cdots+9w^9\). Subtracting \(wS\) from \(S\) changes each interior coefficient from \(k\) to \(k-(k-1)=1\), leaving the final endpoint term:
\[
(1-w)S=(w+w^2+\cdots+w^9)-9w^{10}=-9w.
\]

The modulus of a product is the product of the moduli. This follows directly from the given definition: for \(u=p+qi\) and \(v=r+si\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
|uv|^2&=(pr-qs)^2+(ps+qr)^2\\
&=(p^2+q^2)(r^2+s^2)=|u|^2|v|^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking nonnegative square roots proves the rule. Hence \(|1-w|\,|S|=9\). In particular, \(S\ne0\), so the requested reciprocal exists and equals \(|1-w|/9\).

Finally, using \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) and the cosine double-angle identity,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|1-w|^2
&=(1-\cos40^\circ)^2+\sin^240^\circ\\
&=2-2\cos40^\circ\\
&=4\sin^220^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\sin20^\circ>0\), we obtain \(|1-w|=2\sin20^\circ\). Thus the answer is \(\boxed{\frac29\sin20^\circ}\), choice B.
